facts.statement: Ángel Cabrera described Aristonectes parvidens in 1941 based on a specimen from Chubut Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of A. parvidens was found in the Lefipán Formation and dated to the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was interpreted as an adult or elderly individual.
facts.quote: The specimen was interpreted as an adult, or even an elderly individual

facts.statement: The specific name parvidens means "small teeth", referring to the small size of the tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The specific epithet parvidens means "small teeth", in reference to the rather small size of the tooth sockets

facts.statement: Heavy reconstruction of the original specimen left the precise anatomy of Aristonectes uncertain throughout the 20th century.
facts.quote: Since the unknown parts of the original specimen were heavily reconstructed, the precise anatomy of Aristonectes remained uncertain throughout the 20th century

facts.statement: It is debated whether the holotype of Plesiosaurus chilensis belongs to A. parvidens, with some researchers suggesting it does.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Aristonectes quiriquinensis (SGO.PV.260) was found in Maastrichtian beds of the Quiriquina Formation.
facts.quote: The specimen, cataloged as SGO.PV.260, was found in Maastrichtian beds of the Quiriquina Formation

facts.statement: Two additional specimens from Quiriquina Island were referred to Aristonectes quiriquinensis in 2015.
facts.quote: In 2015, two other specimens from Quiriquina Island were referred to A. quiriquinensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Aristonectes quiriquinensis was redescribed in 2018 following further preparation.
facts.quote: In 2018, the holotype specimen was redescribed after further preparation.

facts.statement: Aristonectes is a plesiosaur that was historically difficult to analyze due to the incompleteness of its fossil remains.
facts.quote: Aristonectes is a plesiosaur that had been particularly difficult for scientists to analyze because of its incompleteness.

facts.statement: Recent research on Aristonectes parvidens and A. quiriquinensis allowed scientists to classify the genus among the elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: Its relationships remained unclear until more recent research carried out on A. parvidens and the discovery of the second species A. quiriquinensis have made it possible to redescribe its anatomy and classify it among the elasmosaurids.

facts.statement: The holotype of Aristonectes quiriquinensis is estimated to be over 10 meters long and weigh nearly 4.2 metric tons.
facts.quote: Aristonectes is a large representative of the plesiosauroids, the holotype of A. quiriquinensis having an estimated total body length of about or more than 10 m long and body mass of nearly 4.2 MT.

facts.statement: A referred specimen of Aristonectes from the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica (MLP 89-III-3-1) is estimated to be between 11 and 11.9 meters long and weigh between 10.7 and 13.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: A referred specimen of Aristonectes discovered in the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica, cataloged as MLP 89-III-3-1, is considered to be one of the largest and heaviest plesiosaurs identified to date, having an estimated size between 11 - 11.9 m long and a body mass of 10.7 - 13.5 MT.

facts.statement: The skulls of both known Aristonectes species are flattened and ogive-shaped.
facts.quote: In the two known species, the skull of Aristonectes is flattened and ogive-shaped.

facts.statement: Around 13 teeth were present in the premaxilla and 50 in the maxilla of Aristonectes quiriquinensis.
facts.quote: Around 13 teeth were present in the premaxilla and 50 in the maxilla.

facts.statement: The dentition of Aristonectes quiriquinensis is homodont, meaning all teeth are of similar shape.
facts.quote: The dentition of A. quiriquinensis, and most likely A. parvidens, is homodont, which means that the teeth are all of similar shape.

facts.statement: The teeth of Aristonectes quiriquinensis have an oval cross-section similar to those of Northern Hemisphere and Weddellian Province elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: The teeth of A. quiriquinensis have an oval cross-section, being very similar to elasmosaurids of the Northern Hemisphere and the Weddellian Province

facts.statement: The best-preserved swim paddle of Aristonectes quiriquinensis is about 3 meters long, indicating a total wingspan of 7 meters.
facts.quote: The best-preserved swim paddle being about 3 m long. Combined with the aforementioned width of the pectoral girdle, this indicates a total wingspan of 7 m.

facts.statement: Aristonectes quiriquinensis lived during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: The specimen, cataloged as SGO.PV.260, was found in Maastrichtian beds of the Quiriquina Formation

facts.statement: A referred specimen of Aristonectes was discovered in the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica.
facts.quote: A referred specimen of Aristonectes discovered in the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica

facts.statement: The curved cervical ribs and neural spines of Aristonectes likely allowed the animal to maintain its trunk higher than its head.
facts.quote: The cervical ribs and cervical neural spines of Aristonectes are curved towards the head, similar to other members of the subfamily Aristonectinae. This morphology would have allowed for maintaining the trunk higher than the head.

facts.statement: The long limbs of Aristonectes are comparable in proportion to the Early Jurassic rhomaleosaurid Meyerasaurus and the modern humpback whale.
facts.quote: In aquatic tetrapods, such limb proportions are only observable in the rhomaleosaurid Meyerasaurus from the Early Jurassic and in the modern humpback whale.

facts.statement: It is likely that Aristonectes quiriquinensis had fewer teeth than A. parvidens, based on the preservation of tooth sockets.
facts.quote: Therefore, it is likely that A. quiriquinensis would have fewer teeth than A. parvidens.

facts.statement: Aristonectes is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of what is now South America and Antarctica.
facts.quote: Aristonectes (nombre que significa "el mejor nadador") es un género extinto de plesiosaurio del Cretácico Superior de lo que ahora es Suramérica y la Antártida.

facts.statement: The type species Aristonectes parvidens was originally named by Cabrera in 1941.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es Aristonectes parvidens, nombrado originalmente por Cabrera en 1941.

facts.statement: Cabrera classified Aristonectes within the family Elasmosauridae in 1941 based on cranial element shape.
facts.quote: In 1941, Cabrera classified it within the Elasmosauridae based on the shape of the cranial elements, which will prove to be correct decades later.

facts.statement: David S. Brown moved Aristonectes into the family Cryptoclididae in 1981 based on having 6 to 15 teeth in the premaxilla.
facts.quote: In 1981, David S. Brown moved Aristonectes into the Cryptoclididae based on the presence of 6 to 15 teeth in the premaxilla.

facts.statement: O'Keefe and Street moved Aristonectes into the newly erected family Aristonectidae in 2009 after finding Cimoliasauridae to be a junior synonym of Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2009, O'Keefe and Hallie P. Street reviewed the validity of Cimoliasauridae, and found that this taxon is a junior synonym of the Elasmosauridae. Therefore, they moved the genera Aristonectes, Kaiwhekea, Kimmerosaurus and Tatenectes into the newly erected family Aristonectidae.

facts.statement: Ketchum and Benson recovered Aristonectes parvidens as an elasmosaurid in 2010, supporting the earlier classification by Gasparini et al. (2003).
facts.quote: Posteriormente Ketchum y Benson (2010) recuperan a Aristonectes parvidens como un Elasmosauridae retomando así las ideas originales de Gasparini et al., 2003.

facts.statement: Otero and colleagues referred Aristonectes to the subfamily Aristonectinae within Elasmosauridae in 2013.
facts.quote: Recientemente Otero et al., 2013 refieren a Kaiwhekea y Aristonectes a la Subfamilia Aristonectinae dentro de los Elasmosauridae.

facts.statement: Aristonectes belongs to the subfamily Aristonectinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Aristonectinae

facts.statement: Aristonectes is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Elasmosauridae

facts.statement: Aristonectes lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Aristonectes is known from Maastrichtian geological formations in Patagonia and Antarctica.
facts.quote: Aristonectes is known from various geological formations of Patagonia and Antarctica that date to the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aristonectes have been found in the Quiriquina and Dorotea formations in Chile, the Allen, Jagüel, and Lefipán formations in Argentina, and the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica.
facts.quote: It is known from the Quiriquina and Dorotea formations in Chile, from the Allen, Jagüel and Lefipán formations in Argentina and from the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica.

facts.statement: Aristonectes was likely endemic to the Weddellian Province, a region formed after Antarctica's isolation.
facts.quote: The presence of Aristonectes within these formations shows that it would have been endemic in the Weddellian Province, a geographical area that appeared after the isolation of Antarctica.

facts.statement: Over 793 gastroliths were found in the largest known specimen of Aristonectes, MLP 89-III-3-1, from Antarctica.
facts.quote: Among these are 5 elements discovered during the second exhumation of the holotype of A. quiriquinensis, and over 793 in the largest known specimen of the genus, MLP 89-III-3-1, from Antarctica.

facts.statement: O'Gorman and colleagues concluded in 2014 that Aristonectes swallowed random batches of sediment containing stones rather than selecting individual gastroliths.
facts.quote: In 2014, O'Gorman and colleagues analysed the gastrolithes of the Antarctica specimen and concluded that Aristonectes did not select individual stones for ingestion, but swallowed batches of sediment at random that contained stones of various sizes.

facts.statement: Aristonectes fed in benthic zones by mixing prey and sediment together.
facts.quote: This indicates that A. quiriquinensis fed in benthic zones, mixing prey and sediment at the same time.

facts.statement: Samuel P. Welles considered Aristonectes to be an indeterminate pliosaur in 1962 due to its enigmatic anatomy.
facts.quote: In 1962, Samuel P. Welles considered Aristonectes to be an indeterminate pliosaur based on its rather enigmatic anatomy.

facts.statement: O'Keefe and colleagues expressed skepticism in 2011 about grouping Aristonectes and Kaiwhekea with Tatenectes due to morphological discrepancies.
facts.quote: In 2011, two years later, O'Keefe and colleagues were skeptical about the classification of Aristonectes and Kaiwhekea with Tatenectes, because their morphologies did not seem to correspond.

facts.statement: It is debated whether mosasaurs in the López de Bertodano Formation attacked contemporary plesiosaurs like Aristonectes.
facts.quote: Some of these mosasaurs could have attacked the contemporary plesiosaurs of the formation, including Aristonectes.
